title: Every Alarm Has a Cause: An Open Generator of Telecom Alarm Storms with Exact Root Causes, Bound to NORIA-O, RFC 8632 and TMF642
abstract: arXiv:2610.30004v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Alarm root-cause analysis is studied on data that cannot be shared. Operator logs are confidential, so what the field publishes is a causal graph between alarm types rather than per-incident causes, a fixed scenario set, gated, or never released. Two recent benchmarks carry per-incident root causes at scale; neither states a download location or a licence.   We give a generator rather than a dataset. It runs on real backbone topologies from the Internet Topology Zoo and records the exact root cause and the propagation path of every alarm -- a by-product of generation, not a labelling pass. Every emitted field binds to a term in NORIA-O, RFC 8632, RFC 8345 or TMF642, and an unknown term fails the run. We ship fixed configurations, splits, a scorer and nine baselines.   A one-line rule -- rank the device that raised the earliest critical alarm -- takes top-1 at 0.650 against 0.575 for our own temporal method, and wins 13 of 15 runs over

translated_title: 每个告警都有原因：一个绑定NORIA-O、RFC 8632和TMF642标准、具有精确根因的开放电信告警风暴生成器
translated_abstract: 告警根因分析的研究一直建立在无法共享的数据之上。运营商日志是保密的，因此该领域发布的内容往往是告警类型之间的因果图，而非逐事件的根因，或者是固定的场景集、受访问限制的、甚至从未发布的数据。最近两个基准测试虽在大规模上包含逐事件根因，但均未说明下载位置或许可证。我们提供的不是数据集，而是一个生成器。它运行在来自Internet Topology Zoo的真实骨干网拓扑之上，并记录每个告警的精确根因及其传播路径——这是生成过程的副产品，而非额外的标注环节。每个输出字段都绑定到NORIA-O、RFC 8632、RFC 8345或TMF642中的术语，任何未知术语都会导致运行失败。我们随附固定的配置、数据划分、评分器和九个基线方法。一条单行规则——对最早发出严重告警的设备进行排序——取得了0.650的top-1准确率，优于我们自己时序方法的0.575，并在15次运行中赢得了13次。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个开源的电信告警风暴生成器，它在真实骨干网拓扑上生成告警并自动附带精确根因与传播路径，所有字段严格绑定NORIA-O、RFC 8632、RFC 8345和TMF642等标准术语，从而解决了告警根因分析领域缺乏可共享、可复现、标准化基准数据的难题。
en_tdlr: This paper presents an open generator of telecom alarm storms that runs on real backbone topologies and records exact per-incident root causes and propagation paths as a by-product of generation, with every field bound to standard terms from NORIA-O, RFC 8632, RFC 8345 and TMF642, addressing the lack of shareable, reproducible and standardized benchmarks for alarm root-cause analysis.
